title: Spawner economy, ranks and progress pace

questions.title: What should cost more: tier or count?
questions.context: Today every tier 1 spawner costs $117,000 and every tier 2 costs $213,000, and every one pays back in 60 hours. You said better spawners should cost more.

options.label: The tier
options.detail: Better tier, higher price: $117,000 for tier 1 up to $1.75M for tier 12, each about 1.28 times the last. The number you own only lowers output, as built.

options.label: Tier and count
options.detail: As a, and each extra spawner of that tier on your island also costs 2% more. Reverses the REVIEW3 F2 decision; alts skip it by buying on another island.

options.label: Only the count
options.detail: One price for every tier that rises with each spawner you own. This is the old +10% plan (642) that F2 replaced; it hits a wall at about 25 spawners.

questions.title: How many spawner tiers?
questions.context: Today there are 5 tiers and the shop sells 2. The Depths have 12 tiers, so one rule is easy to explain: spawner tier N opens with Depths tier N.

options.label: 12, one per Depths tier
options.detail: The 30 mobs are sorted into 12 tiers by what their loot sells for. Prices $117,000 to $1.75M.

options.label: 6 tiers
options.detail: Every second Depths tier (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). Fewer prices to learn, bigger jumps of about x1.65 per tier.

options.label: Keep 5
options.detail: As built. Tiers 3 to 5 stay crate-only and the payback stays a flat 60 hours.

questions.title: Should better spawners spawn faster?
questions.context: A tier 1 spawner makes 144 mobs an hour. If speed grows 8% per tier, tier 12 makes 336 an hour and earns more without needing richer loot.

options.label: Yes, +8% per tier
options.detail: Tier 12 spawns every 4 to 17 seconds instead of 10 to 40. Better means richer mobs and a faster spawner.

options.label: No, same speed
options.detail: Simplest to explain. Vanilla loot tops out near $75 per mob, so tier 12 earns at most $9,200 an hour instead of $14,400.

options.label: Yes, +15% per tier
options.detail: Tier 12 makes about 670 mobs an hour. Income outgrows the price ladder, so payback must rise more, and the server has more spawn work.

questions.title: Hard cap per spawner tier?
questions.context: The 129th spawner of a tier costs full price for 10% output and pays back in 602 hours, so nobody should buy it. A hard cap also keeps mob load down.

options.label: 32 per tier
options.detail: 16 at full output and 16 at 60%; 384 on the island at most. The Spawner Stack Limit upgrade then stops at 32 per block (your S20 said 512). The credit perk can add up to +64.

options.label: 64 per tier
options.detail: Adds 32 more at 35%; stack limit stops at 64 per block. With every upgrade maxed, spawners reach 37% of a late regular's income, above the 25% alert line.

options.label: No hard cap, as built
options.detail: The 65th to 128th work at 20% and the 129th and later at 10% (payback 300 to 600 h). The stack limit upgrade keeps 8 to 512 and the money sink it gives.

questions.title: What unlocks buying a spawner tier?
questions.context: Today anyone can buy a tier 2 spawner for $213,000 on day 1. A gate makes the ladder a progression.

options.label: Your best Depths tier
options.detail: Tier N needs Depths tier N (Mine, Forest or Combat, whichever is best). A regular player: tier 2 at 2 h, tier 4 at 9 h, tier 8 at 52 h.

options.label: Island level
options.detail: For example tier N needs island level 4 x N. Island level will change (new divisor and sources), so the gate moves later.

options.label: Both
options.detail: Depths tier and island level. Two rules to explain and two numbers to tune.

options.label: No gate, price only
options.detail: As today. A rich player buys the best tier at once.

questions.title: Who sells spawner tiers 9 to 12?
questions.context: Late players earn $27M to $36M an hour, so a $1.75M spawner costs them 3 minutes of income. Money alone cannot make the top tiers feel expensive.

options.label: Black Market for shards
options.detail: 15 / 25 / 40 / 60 shards for tiers 9 to 12 (a late regular earns 5 to 10 shards a day), plus crates. /shop sells tiers 1 to 8 for money.

options.label: /shop for money, all 12
options.detail: Simple, but tiers 9 to 12 cost under 3 minutes of late income, so the price means nothing.

options.label: Crates and the auction house only
options.detail: No shop price. The AH sets the price and luck decides who has one.

questions.title: How big may late spawners get?
questions.context: Spawner loot is vanilla and each item has one price, so the best mob pays about $75 per kill. At that ceiling all 12 tiers at the cap earn 5% of a late regular's income, or 26% with every spawner upgrade maxed.

options.label: A small helper
options.detail: Stay vanilla (R3-21a): spawners are an early-to-mid engine at 8% to 25% of income and the Depths stay the main source.

options.label: A real pillar
options.detail: A custom 'essence' loot item per tier (sellable, not craftable, not in /shop) could lift spawners to 40% of income. Reverses R3-21a and needs a model rerun.

options.label: Bigger by upgrades only
options.detail: Spawner Rate and Mob Loot go from +12% to +20% per level, so the two together reach x9 instead of x4.8. No new item; upgrade prices rise too.

questions.title: What about mobs that earn nothing?
questions.context: Squid, glow squid, magma cube, piglin, zombified piglin, shulker, ravager and breeze earn under $10 per mob because their drops (ink, magma cream, saddle, breeze rod) cannot be sold. The squid spawner costs $213,000 today.

options.label: Take them out for now
options.detail: Hidden from /shop, crates and the Black Market until each gets a sellable drop. Spawners already owned keep working.

options.label: Give them sellable drops
options.detail: You pick a special drop for each (D4, R3-21a) and a price for it: about 8 new prices.

options.label: Keep as cheap decoration
options.detail: Sold cheaply and labelled 'No sellable loot'. They fill the tiers but never pay back.

questions.title: How fast should better spawners pay back?
questions.context: Today every tier pays back in 60 production hours (5 days for a regular). The proposal adds 5 hours per tier.

options.label: Gently: 60 h to 122 h
options.detail: Tier 1 pays back in 60 h, tier 12 in 122 h at full output; price grows about 1.28 times per tier. The 17th to 32nd take 100 to 203 h.

options.label: Steeply: 60 h to 200 h
options.detail: Top tiers are luxury items: tier 12 costs $2.9M and pays back in 200 h (17 days for a regular). Fewer players buy them.

options.label: Flat 60 h, as today
options.detail: Every tier is an equally good deal, so players always buy the best tier they can afford.

questions.title: Names of the 7 donor ranks?
questions.context: Your answer 386 asked for themed names and 7 ranks. The names Hatchling to Immortal were only suggested, never confirmed. Crate names (Ember, Cinder, Blaze, Inferno, Phoenix, Eclipse, Conqueror) are avoided.

options.label: Phoenix life
options.detail: Hatchling, Fledgling, Firewing, Flamecrest, Sunfeather, Pyrelord, Immortal: one story, a phoenix growing up.

options.label: Rising fire
options.detail: Spark, Kindle, Flare, Wildfire, Firestorm, Sunfire, Ascendant. Spark clashes with a free tag.

options.label: Flame keepers
options.detail: Kindler, Flamekeeper, Firebrand, Pyromancer, Sunforged, Starfire, Eternal. Sounds like classes, not ranks.

options.label: You write them
options.detail: I keep the structure, colours and prices and you give the 7 names.

questions.title: Names of the free and won ranks?
questions.context: The free rank shows [Ember] and [Ashborn] in different places today, and Ember is also a crate name. Won season ranks copy a donor tier's perks for one season.

options.label: Ashborn; Torchbearer, Flameheart, Firecrown
options.detail: Free rank Ashborn ('born from the ash'). Won ranks: Torchbearer (copies Fledgling), Flameheart (Flamecrest), Firecrown (Pyrelord).

options.label: Tinder; Cinderguard, Blazeheart, Skycrown
options.detail: Avoids crate words but Tinder is less phoenix, and Spark-like names clash with free tags.

options.label: You write them
options.detail: I keep the structure and you give the 4 names.

questions.title: Credit prices of the 7 ranks?
questions.context: The top rank is 13,500 credits (about $125). 100 credits is about $1; packs are 500 = $5, 1,000 = $10, 2,700 = $25, 14,000 = $130. An upgrade pays only the difference.

options.label: Cheap start
options.detail: 500 / 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,500 / 5,500 / 8,500 / 13,500. More buyers on the first rank, less money from each.

options.label: Late-heavy
options.detail: 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,500 / 5,000 / 7,500 / 10,000 / 13,500. The first ranks cost more and the gaps get smaller.

questions.title: Does a bought rank give any progress?
questions.context: R3-7 says bought ranks give 0% sell and 0% skill XP, but your principle 9 said 'some progress, to a degree'. The old plan had up to +15% sell and +10% skill XP.

options.label: No: looks and convenience
options.detail: Perks: looks, commands, AH, loadout and vault slots and a bound weekly kit of food, blocks and a little fuel. Safest under Mojang's rules.

options.label: Tiny and capped
options.detail: +1% to +5% sell and +1% to +3% XP on the top ranks only, inside the +300% cap. The Mojang risk grows.

options.label: As the old plan
options.detail: +2% to +15% sell and +1% to +10% XP. About 14% more income early and 7% late, and the biggest Mojang risk.

questions.title: How should staff badges read?
questions.context: You listed OWNER, ADMIN, MOD, HELPER, BUILDER in bold. Players see [Owner] and [Moderator] in mixed case, not bold, today.

options.label: [MOD] bold caps
options.detail: [OWNER] [ADMIN] [MOD] [HELPER] [BUILDER] bold in your colours. Donors stay normal case, so staff and donors never look alike.

options.label: [Moderator] bold, mixed case
options.detail: Same colours and bold, full words. Longer on a phone.

options.label: Caps in tab, words in chat
options.detail: Two looks for one rank. More to keep in sync.

questions.title: When does a player become Ashborn?
questions.context: Today /freerank needs 30 minutes of play and gives the group Ember, and everyone else already shows [Ashborn]. Principle 4 says the tutorial unlocks the game.

options.label: Automatically after the tutorial
options.detail: Ashborn arrives when the tutorial ends. Before that the badge reads [New] in grey. /freerank only picks the free tag.

options.label: /freerank after the tutorial
options.detail: One click after the tutorial. Players who never click stay [New].

options.label: 30 minutes played, as built
options.detail: Keeps a playtime gate that principle 4 replaced.

questions.title: Which ranks include a free profile slot?
questions.context: Profile slot 2 costs 500 credits and slot 3 costs 1,500 (B17-R1-15). Firewing costs 2,700, so a slot inside it is worth 500 of that.

options.label: Firewing and Pyrelord
options.detail: Slot 2 from Firewing (3rd rank), slot 3 from Pyrelord (6th).

options.label: Flamecrest and Immortal
options.detail: Slot 2 from Flamecrest (4th), slot 3 from Immortal only. Slots stay a stronger reason to buy credits.

options.label: None
options.detail: Slots only for credits (500 and 1,500). A rank never includes one.

questions.title: What does a donor get every month?
questions.context: R3-8 says a bought rank gives one monthly cosmetic instead of crate keys. The old plan also had a weekly bound kit of food, blocks and a little island fuel.

options.label: Monthly cosmetic and weekly kit
options.detail: One cosmetic from a list you write (claim after 5 h played that month) and a bound weekly kit sized S to XL. One click in /menu, Rank rewards.

options.label: Monthly cosmetic only
options.detail: Simplest. No kit and nothing to hand out each week.

options.label: Cosmetic and a bigger kit
options.detail: The top ranks' kit also carries 3 hours of island fuel (capped by the fuel tank). Still no keys and no money.

questions.title: Which pacing model?
questions.context: Today a regular player gets a reward every 5 minutes in the first hour but only every 98 minutes in month 2 to 3, and the tutorial gives no level-up.

options.label: Balanced
options.detail: Cheaper first levels, island level doubled, a reward every 3 min in the first hour and every 45 min late. Season income +5% to +10%.

options.label: Fast and generous
options.detail: A reward every 2 min at the start, island level x3.3, tier 4 at 4 h. Income +12% to +18%; grinders run out of things near day 40.

options.label: Slow burn
options.detail: Keep today's numbers. The empty first minutes and the flat late season stay.

questions.title: Tutorial length and reward?
questions.context: Today: 11 steps, about 3 minutes, $2,500 + 25 crystals + a title. One hour of play pays $53,000, and the steps pay nothing by themselves.

options.label: Same steps, a reward on each
options.detail: 11 steps in 4 to 5 real minutes. Each step pays a few hundred money or crystals. Finish: $7,500, 50 crystals, a bound Ember key and the first levels.

options.label: Longer and bigger
options.detail: 11 steps plus 5 quick wins (skills, upgrade, enchant, shop, sell), about 6 minutes. Finish: $10,000, 75 crystals and a key.

options.label: Keep as built
options.detail: 3 minutes, $2,500 and 25 crystals.

questions.title: How many levels does the tutorial give?
questions.context: The mine step needs 15 of the 600 Mining XP for level 1, so you finish the tutorial at level 0 in everything.

options.label: Five quick level-ups
options.detail: Mining 1, tool level 2, mining pillar 2, island level 1. One-time XP gifts to the profile, no money.

options.label: Eight
options.detail: Mining 2, tool 3, pillar 3, island 1. Depths tier 2 then opens at about 45 minutes.

options.label: None, only rewards
options.detail: Levels come from play only. The tutorial pays money and crystals.

questions.title: How soon is the first new Depths tier?
questions.context: Tier 2 (Copper) opens at Mining 5, which takes a regular player 2.2 hours. The first hour has no unlock at all.

options.label: At about 1 hour
options.detail: Early levels cost 40% of today: Mining 5 at 1.1 h, tier 4 at 5.6 h, tier 8 at 43 h.

options.label: At about 45 minutes
options.detail: Early levels cost 25%: tier 2 at 0.75 h, tier 4 at 4 h, tier 8 at 36 h.

options.label: Keep 2.2 hours
options.detail: As built. The first hour stays without an unlock.

questions.title: How many island levels?
questions.context: Island level is points divided by 10: 38 at month 1 and 70 at season end for a regular. Titles and achievements use those numbers (Architect at 50).

options.label: Points / 5
options.detail: The numbers double: 77 at month 1, 140 at the end (casual 80, grinder 210). Every level is half the work and the thresholds double.

options.label: Points / 3
options.detail: 128 at month 1 and 233 at the end. Every level is a third of the work, but the numbers get big.

options.label: Points / 10, as built
options.detail: 70 at the end. Island level rises slowly in steps of 10 points.

questions.title: How often should the game reward you?
questions.context: Measured today for a regular player: every 5.5 min in the first hour, 4.6 min on day 1, 10 min in week 1, 32 min in month 1 and 98 min in month 2 to 3.

options.label: 3 / 6 / 12 / 25 / 45 minutes
options.detail: By stage: first hour, day 1, week 1, month 1, month 2 to 3. Late steps use Ascension, masteries and achievements as medium moments.

options.label: 2 / 4 / 8 / 15 / 30 minutes
options.detail: A reward almost always in sight. More popups and more sound, with a risk of noise.

options.label: As today
options.detail: No target; the late season keeps its 98-minute gaps.

questions.title: How big is a level-up moment?
questions.context: Today a level-up is a title, a sound and a chat line, the same size for level 3 and level 50.

options.label: Three sizes
options.detail: Small: action-bar line and soft sound. Medium (every 5th level, new tier): title, sound, flame ring. Big (every 25th, tier 8+): fanfare, burst, island chat. One setting: Full, Quiet, Off.

options.label: One size for all
options.detail: Title, sound and particles on every level. Simple, but 20 popups an hour would be noisy.

options.label: Text only
options.detail: Action bar and chat lines, no titles or particles. Cleanest and least rewarding.

questions.title: What should a maxed player do?
questions.context: After all 161 upgrade levels and 67 mastery ranks a player has Ascension: endless levels worth 1.5 island points each that keep money draining.

options.label: Keep Ascension, smaller steps
options.detail: Endless Ascension as designed. Every level is a medium popup and every 10th gets a title. It is the late reward rhythm.

options.label: Add a prestige star
options.detail: A cosmetic star per 25 Ascension levels next to your name and in /is top. No reset and no power, but a new small system.

options.label: Nothing more
options.detail: Grinders have nothing to chase after tier 12 on day 51, and the sheet needs the late sink.

questions.title: Help for players who start late?
questions.context: A profile created on day 40 of a 90-day season starts at level 0 like everyone else and its island is far behind the top.

options.label: Rookie boost
options.detail: From day 14, a new profile gets x1.5 skill, tool and pillar XP for its first 10 played hours, fading to x1. No money and nothing tradeable.

options.label: No help
options.detail: Profiles are islands. Late starters learn the same curve and the next season gives everyone a fresh start.

options.label: Bigger catch-up
options.detail: x2 XP for 25 hours and the median player's Depths tier unlocked. Faster, but it blurs the top lists.

questions.title: How far should a casual player get?
questions.context: A casual player (1 hour a day) reaches Depths tier 8 on day 68 and earns about $130M in the season. A regular reaches tier 10 on day 54.

options.label: Tier 8 around day 55
options.detail: Slightly faster with Balanced pacing: tier 4 on day 7, tier 8 on day 55. A tier unlock about every week.

options.label: Tier 8 on day 68
options.detail: As built; only the early levels get faster.

options.label: Tier 10 by season end
options.detail: Casuals see two more tiers. Needs tier gaps 30% shorter late, which changes the whole economy sheet.
